_meta.indication: Add-on maintenance treatment of adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with severe asthma

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of tezepelumab 210 mg SC Q4W vs placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and adolescent patients aged 12-80 years with severe, uncontrolled asthma, enrolled regardless of baseline eosinophil count
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annualized asthma exacerbation rate (AAER) over 52 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: AAER reduced by 56% vs placebo (RR 0.44; 95% CI 0.37, 0.53; p<0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dose-ranging trial (70 mg Q4W, 210 mg Q4W, 280 mg Q2W vs placebo)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults aged 18-75 years with severe, uncontrolled asthma
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annualized asthma exacerbation rate measured at Week 52
pivotal_trials.n: 550 treated (placebo 138; 70 mg Q4W 138; 210 mg Q4W 137; 280 mg Q2W 137)
pivotal_trials.result: At the 210 mg Q4W dose, exacerbation rate ratio vs placebo 0.29 (95% CI 0.16, 0.51; p<0.001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=3%) were pharyngitis (4% vs 3%), arthralgia (4% vs 3%), and back pain (4% vs 3%); injection site reactions occurred in 3.3% vs 2.7% placebo
target_moa: Tezepelumab is a human IgG2 monoclonal antibody that binds thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP), preventing its interaction with the TSLP receptor and modulating the downstream Th2 inflammatory pathway in asthma
companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic; the CDRH review addressed only the pre-filled syringe device constituent of the combination product

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee was convened; the review team did not identify issues that would benefit from AdCom discussion

basis.text: Granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation in September 2018 based on the phase 2b PATHWAY trial, showing preliminary efficacy in severe asthma patients with and without an eosinophilic phenotype

citations.quote: Tezepelumab was granted Breakthrough Drug Designation in September 2018 because it showed preliminary efficacy in asthma patients not only with eosinophilic phenotype, but in asthma patients without an eosinophilic phenotype, i.e. a broader asthma population.
